facts.claim: Reverse the horizontal part alone and it carries on.
facts.problem: Wrong. An inclination compass reads which end of the field axis dips into the ground, so flipping the horizontal component alone (vertical still pointing down) makes the dipping end point the other way and the bird reverses, just as a polarity compass would. The condition that leaves the bird unchanged, and the one Wiltschko used to show polarity is ignored, is reversing BOTH components (a full polarity flip of the field). [P9 S7] is right; [P9 S8] should read roughly: reverse the whole field, both parts at once, and it carries on.
